answer: Garden-path quorum routing. Each new agent must attach to a randomly assigned neighborhood whose existing members counter-sign its routing edge; fake identities cluster locally but cannot span the graph, so a sybil swarm gets quarantined into a low-trust lotus of isolated subgraphs. An attacker pays one live, latency-bearing handshake per forged node plus repeated re-attachment as neighbors rotate, making each identity cost real bandwidth and uptime rather than a one-time fee. Signatures are logged with a quill into a public edge ledger.
